texts: bad: "the whole cliff base" has no carrier for the totality, so the translator files it as a property and the parse ends up asserting that the cliff base is whole/intact — something the sentence never says — while the only compliant alternative is to drop "whole" and lose the coverage claim entirely. Rewrite the totality as a universal over the parts, which does have a licensed and fireable form: "Tessa Brae walks every part of the cliff base each morning during molting weeks." Everything else — the cliff/base part-whole split, "each morning", and the molting-weeks frame — parses correctly and needs no change.

good. the definite plural subject gets a group plus a fireable per-member rule, "pick up" is kept whole as a phrasal verb, and "molted" is distributed over the individual feathers rather than fused into the kind.
good. the group subject, the feathers as unchanged content, and the "into"-destination all land in the right slots, and the per-member rule is fireable.

bad: "each morning's collection" is a possessive inside the object, but the translator re-reads it as an adverbial and asserts when and how often the recording happens (every morning, once a day) — a timing the sentence never states about the recording — while the per-morning universal itself stays unencoded. Put the frequency on the verb, where it is licensed: "The collectors record the collection in a Watch ledger each morning." That states outright the daily recurrence of the recording, which the original only implied through the genitive.
good. the definite plurals take group witnesses, "feather bin" fuses with its head genus, the bin is the destination of the adding, and the per-member rule is fireable.
